options: To write compressed flight logs to the SD card
To fuse noisy sensors into one estimate
To keep the link to the GCS
To drive the motors
questions.explain: One consistent estimate of position, velocity, and attitude: a prediction from the IMU, corrected by infrequent GPS, baro, and compass measurements.

options: Changing the video transmitter channel on interference
Moving to a healthier EKF core
Switching to a backup mission
Changing the flight mode automatically
questions.explain: Each IMU gets its own EKF core; the healthiest one is used.

options: Yaw from the compass
Yaw from GPS velocity (GSF)
Yaw is not estimated
Yaw from an external navigation system
questions.explain: It works only when moving: on the ground there is no yaw.

questions.q: What do you do about a pre-arm "EKF compass variance"?
options: Raise FS_EKF_THRESH to 1.0 and take off
Look for interference and check the calibration
Disable the EKF check
Take off, it will clear by itself
questions.explain: Interference, calibration, compass orientation. The threshold is not the fix.

options: Only report to the GCS
Land if the mode requires position
Switch to AltHold
Land from all modes, even Stabilize
questions.explain: 0 is report only, 1 is Land if the mode requires position, 2 is AltHold, 3 is Land always.

questions.q: Why was EKF3 disabled in the HeeWing case?
options: EKF3 does not support the QuadPlane configuration
No compass and an unstable GPS
The flight controller ran out of memory
The loop runs faster that way
questions.explain: No compass and an unstable GPS, so DCM and the modes that need no position were chosen: a deliberate trade-off for specific hardware.

options: The compass is healthy and calibrated
The compass is being rejected by the gate
The GPS signal is lost
The barometer reports the wrong altitude
questions.explain: The ratio of the innovation to the allowed one is > 1: interference or calibration.

options: The radius of the circular geofence around home
The threshold for resetting position to the GPS
The width of the compass gate
The required RTK accuracy
questions.explain: The disagreement with the GPS beyond which the position is reset to the GPS. Larger tolerates glitches better, but lets the position wander longer.

questions.q: An XKF4 fragment during position jerks. What is happening?
options: The GPS velocity and position test ratios are > 1, so the EKF is rejecting GPS: a glitch or multipath
SH around 0.3 means the barometer is rejected and the height comes from GPS only
SM around 0.2 is a sign of magnetic interference: the compass is rejected, hence the position jerks
Values above 1 mean the filter is highly confident in the GPS, and the position jerks come from wind gusts
questions.explain: A test ratio > 1 means the measurement did not pass the gate; here that is SV and SP, that is, GPS.
